# Overview

This document contains the final analysis and graphs of the pak choi seed data.

This analysis was performed using  `r version$version.string`. The *tidyverse*
suite of packages was used for data manipulation and visualisation. The
*emmeans* package was used for model predictions. 
The *DHARMa* package was used to help assess model diagnostics and goodness-of-fit.

The predicted 95% confidence intervals and post-hoc pairwise comparison p-values
are adjusted using the FDR correction to account for multiple tests.

# Data used (how it was summarised)

+ The original data is grouped by Year, Farm, Type_of_farm, Boundary_type, Native_new_age, Treatment, Rep.     
+ The mean of the `Seed viable` is taken. This is the mean across all the pods for each rep. Note the number of pods for each Rep was quite variable.  
+ Then the data is grouped by Year, Farm, Type_of_farm, Boundary_type, Native_new_age, Treatment.  
+ The mean seeds viable is calculated, so we get a mean over the Reps.  
+ For each Year, Farm and Boundary_type combination we have a mean seed count for each treatment where each rep has the same weight in the mean.  
+ If we didn't do the means with the two group_by steps then each pod would have the same weight in the mean.  
+ I've assumed that the number of pods is a feature of the pak choi plants and nothing to do with the Treatments.  

<br>

```{r}
load(file="Cleaned_datasets/pc_seed_data_summarised_cleaned.rda")
  
pc_sum <- pc_sum %>% mutate(Treatment=fct_recode(Treatment, "HP"="Hand pollinated"),
                            Simplified_Boundary=fct_recode(Simplified_Boundary, 
                                        "Old SNH"="Old native",
                                        "New SNH"="New native"),
                            Year=fct_recode(Year,
                                            "Year 2021-22"="2021-2022",
                                            "Year 2022-23"="2022-2023",
                                            "Year 2023-24"="2023-2024"),
                            Native_new_age=fct_recode(Native_new_age,
                                                      "Control farm"="Off-farm bare fence",
                                                      "Bare fence"="On-farm bare fence",
                                                      "One-year old new SNH"="One-year old native",
                                                      "Two-year old new SNH"="Two-year old native",
                                                      "Three-year old new SNH"="Three-year old native",
                                                      "Old SNH"="Old native"
                                                      ),
                            Simplified_Boundary=fct_relevel(Simplified_Boundary,
                                                      "Control farm",
                                                      "Bare fence",
                                                      "New SNH",
                                                      "Old SNH"
                                                      ),
                            Type_of_farm=fct_recode(Type_of_farm, "Cropping"="Arable"),
                            Site=factor(paste(as.character(Farm), as.character(Simplified_Boundary), sep=":"))) %>%
  mutate(Native_new_age=fct_relevel(Native_new_age, "Control farm", "Bare fence", "One-year old new SNH", 
                                    "Two-year old new SNH", "Three-year old new SNH", "Old SNH")) %>%
  rename(Boundary_type=Simplified_Boundary) %>%
  mutate(Mean_seeds_viable_rounded = round(Mean_seeds_viable, 0))

str(pc_sum, vec.len = 3) 
```

We next remove the data with 'one-year old new SNH' and 'two-year old new SNH' in 2023-24 is removed. So 'New native' only has

+ One year old in 2021-22  
+ Two year old in 2022-23  
+ Three year old in 2023-24  

Note that is data is all from Arable/Cropping farms (Garrickfield and Limbrick), and there are only 4 observations removed.

Tables of counts before and after the observations are removed are below:

```{r}
# str(pc_mod)
table(pc_sum$Year, pc_sum$Native_new_age) %>% kable(format = "pandoc")
pc_sum <- pc_sum %>% filter( !( (Native_new_age %in% c("One-year old new SNH", "Two-year old new SNH")) & Year=="Year 2023-24" ) ) %>% droplevels()
table(pc_sum$Year, pc_sum$Native_new_age) %>% kable(format = "pandoc")

str(pc_sum, vec.len = 3) 
```

# Modelling comments

+ We remove the Closed treatment from the data.
+ There is no data for Arable/Cropping farms, Off-farm bare fence, 2021-22, Closed.  
+ The Closed is a control and we can see it "worked" in the graph above.  

```{r}
pc_mod <- pc_sum %>% 
  filter(Treatment != "Closed") %>% 
  droplevels()
```

# Model (LMM with 4-way interaction: Y x T_F x T x B_T)

## Description

We fit linear mixed-effects models to the data. The response is
Mean_seeds_viable. The fixed-effects are Year, Type_of_farm, Treatment and
Boundary_type plus their four-way interaction. There is also a random
effect for Farm. The residuals were inspected visually and the
simulateResiduals() function from the DHARMa package was used. There was no
evidence of non-normality, dispersion or outliers.

Note that a Poisson or negative-binomial model did not fit the data well. 

## Diagnostics and ANOVA table

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
#shapiro.test(pc_mod$Mean_seeds_viable) # okay
#hist(pc_mod$Mean_seeds_viable, breaks=30)
mod.lm <- lmer(Mean_seeds_viable ~ Type_of_farm*Treatment*Boundary_type*Year + (1|Site), data=pc_mod)
# AIC(mod.lm); BIC(mod.lm)
residplot(mod.lm, newwd = FALSE)
# summary(mod.lm)
simres <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod.lm)
plot(simres)
# rm(simres)
# mod.lm <- glmmTMB(Mean_seeds_viable_rounded ~ Type_of_farm*Treatment*Boundary_type*Year + (1|Site), family = poisson(link="log"),  data = pc_mod)
# AIC(mod.lm); BIC(mod.lm)
# mod.lm <- glmmTMB(Mean_seeds_viable_rounded ~ 
#                     Type_of_farm*Treatment*Boundary_type + 
#                     Type_of_farm*Treatment*Year + 
#                     Type_of_farm*Boundary_type*Year + 
#                     Treatment*Boundary_type*Year +
#                     (1|Site), family = poisson(link="log"),  data = pc_mod)
# AIC(mod.lm); BIC(mod.lm)
# 
# mod.lm <- glmmTMB(Mean_seeds_viable ~ 
#                     Type_of_farm*Treatment + 
#                     Type_of_farm*Boundary_type + 
#                     Type_of_farm*Year + 
#                     Treatment*Boundary_type + 
#                     Treatment*Year + 
#                     Boundary_type*Year + 
#                     (1|Site), family = poisson(link="log"),  data = pc_mod)
# AIC(mod.lm); BIC(mod.lm)
# residplot(mod.lm, newwd = FALSE)
# summary(mod.lm)
# simres <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod.lm)
# plot(simres)

kable(Anova(mod.lm),digits=6, format = "pandoc")
```

<br>

The Kolmogorov–Smirnov test is not a big deal when there are 214 observations. The residuals look fine.

The four-way and all three-way interactions are not significant. Type_of_farm
is not significant in any of the interactions or as a main effect. Year is only
significant as a main effect. The two-way interaction of Treatment and
Boundary_type is significant. The other two-way interactions are not
significant.

## Predictions of significant effects

### Boundary_type x Treatment by Year

```{r, fig.width=8}
emmip(mod.lm, Boundary_type ~ Treatment | Year, 
      tlab=" ",
      xlab="", 
      ylab="Predicted mean number\nof viable seeds", 
      type = "response", CIs = TRUE, adjust="fdr") + theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors)  

# emm <- emmeans(mod.lm, ~Boundary_type|Treatment:Year, adjust="fdr") 
# emm %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
#   dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
#   rename(`Predicted mean`=emmean) %>%
#   kable(format="pandoc", digits=1)
# 
# contrast(emm, method="pairwise", adjust="fdr", type = "response") %>%
#   as.data.frame() %>% 
#   dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
#   kable(format="pandoc", digits=3)
```

### Boundary_type x Treatment two-way interaction

```{r}
emmip(mod.lm, Boundary_type ~ Treatment,
      tlab=" ",
      xlab="", 
      ylab="Predicted mean number\nof viable seeds", 
      type = "response", CIs = TRUE, adjust="fdr") + theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors)  

emm <- emmeans(mod.lm, ~Boundary_type|Treatment, adjust="fdr") 
contrast(emm, method="pairwise", adjust="fdr", type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
  kable(format="pandoc", digits=3)

emm <- emmeans(mod.lm, ~Treatment|Boundary_type, adjust="fdr") 
contrast(emm, method="pairwise", adjust="fdr", type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
  kable(format="pandoc", digits=3)
```

### Year main effect


```{r, fig.width=4, fig.height=3, out.width = "50%", out.height="50%"}
emmip(mod.lm, ~Year,
      xlab="", 
      ylab="Predicted mean number\nof viable seeds", 
      type = "response", CIs = TRUE, adjust = "fdr") + theme_bw()

emm <- emmeans(mod.lm, ~Year, adjust="fdr") 
contrast(emm, method="pairwise", adjust="fdr", type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
  kable(format="pandoc", digits=3)
```

## Predictions with Type_of_farm

```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
emmip(mod.lm, Boundary_type ~ Treatment | Year:Type_of_farm, 
      tlab=" ",
      xlab="", 
      ylab="Predicted mean number of viable seeds", 
      type = "response", CIs = TRUE, adjust="fdr") + theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors)  

emm <- emmeans(mod.lm, ~Treatment|Boundary_type:Type_of_farm:Year, adjust="fdr")
emm %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
  rename(`Predicted mean`=emmean) %>%
  kable(format="pandoc", digits=1)

contrast(emm, method="pairwise", adjust="fdr", type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(-SE, -df) %>%
  kable(format="pandoc", digits=3)
```
